body:
Pass 14. Verified both closures. Epic 0A subtraction is exactly right - the five unreachable exports gone, the three live ones kept, .evaluate_edge_operation removed entirely, no over-deletion (kept reducers still have 16 test refs). Suite 1617 pass / 0 fail. And Epic 4 verified at pass 11. I am recommending closure of bd-01KZXEVFW3X074685EXWJZNP2D - both halves resolved.

New p2, bd-01KZXJMDRC6VKYX6SA38R0AAH1: Epic 0A closed without the subtraction receipt its own acceptance requires, and the deleted code was never in git. git log --all confirms neither R/operations.R nor test-edge-operations.R was ever committed, and there are no stashes - so ~725 removed lines (347-line test file deleted outright, 287 lines out of operations.R) cannot be audited or restored. That is the exact scenario the blocker note on this epic warned about.

Engineering call was right; the evidence trail is missing. Worth writing the receipt from whatever record remains, and committing before the next epic that deletes anything.

Glad you picked up C6 - the canonical-accumulation prototype and the fix-the-GEMM-shape rule are in the decision note there.
